stories.title: Lindsay Clancy Scheduled for Retrial in March 2027 for Children's Deaths
stories.summary: Lindsay Clancy is set to face a retrial on March 29, 2027, regarding the deaths of her three children, following a previous trial that ended in a mistrial due to a jury deadlock. Prosecutors are pursuing murder charges, while Clancy's defense claims she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time of the incident.

stories.title: Robert Pattinson Announced as the New James Bond
stories.summary: Robert Pattinson has been officially named as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig in the iconic role. This announcement by Amazon MGM Studios ends years of speculation regarding the future of the franchise following Craig's departure after five films. Pattinson, known for his roles in major franchises such as 'The Batman', 'Harry Potter', and 'Twilight', is set to become the seventh actor to portray the legendary spy.

stories.title: Nvidia Board Uninterested in Jensen Huang's Return Amid Support from Trump
stories.summary: The Nvidia board has reportedly expressed no interest in reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO or in any other role at the company. This comes as a campaign to bring Huang back gains traction, with support from several tech figures and notable endorsements, including comments from Donald Trump, who stated he would not mind Huang's return. Huang was ousted following allegations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

stories.title: EU Countries Establish Migrant Deportation Centre in Rwanda
stories.summary: Five EU nations, including Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece, and the Netherlands, have announced plans to create a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda. This facility, described as a 'return hub' for failed asylum seekers, marks the first such initiative outside the European Union. The move aims to facilitate the return of migrants without legal residency in Europe, although it is expected to face legal challenges and criticism from human rights groups.

stories.title: California Files Lawsuit Against OpenAI Over Cybersecurity Concerns
stories.summary: California has initiated a lawsuit against OpenAI, citing the company's failure to implement adequate safeguards in its AI models, which allegedly led to the 'Hugging Face' cyberattack. Attorney General Rob Bonta stated that the attack was predictable due to OpenAI's poor security practices. The lawsuit emphasizes the risks posed to public safety by the company's rapid development of AI technologies without proper monitoring.

stories.title: Seventeen Dead in Two Mass Shootings in South Africa
stories.summary: Seventeen people were killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, occurring in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal provinces. The first incident involved six men and three women found shot dead inside a shack near Pretoria. Police have not yet established motives for the shootings, which took place approximately 530 kilometers apart.

stories.title: Czechs Protest Government's Media Funding Overhaul in Large Numbers
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on November 15 against a government proposal to cut public media fees and shift funding to the state budget. Critics argue that this change threatens the independence and viability of public broadcasters. Protesters expressed concerns that the lack of safeguards against political influence could undermine democracy, drawing parallels to historical events like the Velvet Revolution of 1989.

stories.title: Gérard Depardieu Withdraws Appeal and Apologizes for Sexual Assault Conviction
stories.summary: Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021. In a written statement, the 77-year-old actor acknowledged his guilt and expressed sincere apologies to the victims, stating he had previously hidden behind provocation and humor. The appeal was withdrawn on the day it was scheduled to go to trial.

This outbreak is the deadliest among the country's 17 recorded outbreaks and is on track to exceed the death toll of the West African outbreak that claimed 11,000 lives between 2014 and 2016.
